<reason>CON won the decisive clash: outstanding, completable duties versus irreparable family absence as a permanent bar to closure. PRO’s bloodline frame was morally sharper, but after conceding assessment of demonstrated losses, redaction, and survivor control of intimate details, it never specified an endpoint a government could meet. CON absorbed the reasonable repair claims (records, care, descendant assessment, controlled access) while showing that “designed absence unrepaired” makes finality impossible precisely where harm is greatest, giving the cleaner reason to reject the proposition as written.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>CON Rebuttal 2: turning PRO’s “demonstrated lineage losses…assessed” into a bounded, dischargeable remedy, then showing that treating every remaining family gap as still-open injury erases any meaningful completion test.</best_rebuttal>
